FRENCH — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #19
====

GRADE: Grade 7
SUBJECT: FRENCH
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Active listening 1.4 Listening for information, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Active listening 1.4 Listening for information.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Active listening 1.4 Listening for information.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Active listening 1.4 Listening for information.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Active listening 1.4 Listening for information.

2. When practising Oral Expression Clarity Intonation Pacing, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Oral Expression Clarity Intonation Pacing.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Oral Expression Clarity Intonation Pacing.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Oral Expression Clarity Intonation Pacing.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Oral Expression Clarity Intonation Pacing.

3. The French word for “book” is: (1 mark)
   A. porte
   B. livre
   C. fenêtre
   D. chaise

4. When practising Interactive Speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Interactive Speaking.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Interactive Speaking.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive Speaking.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Interactive Speaking.

5. When practising Interactive Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)

7. When practising Oral Expression Clarity Intonation Tone, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Oral Expression Clarity Intonation Tone.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Oral Expression Clarity Intonation Tone.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Oral Expression Clarity Intonation Tone.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Oral Expression Clarity Intonation Tone.

8. When practising Active Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Active Listening.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Active Listening.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Active Listening.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Active Listening.

9. “Bonjour” is used to say: (1 mark)
   A. Excuse me
   B. Good night only
   C. Thank you
   D. Good morning / hello

10. When practising Active Listening Attention Engagement Vocabulary, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Active Listening Attention Engagement Vocabulary.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Active Listening Attention Engagement Vocabulary.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Active Listening Attention Engagement Vocabulary.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Active Listening Attention Engagement Vocabulary.

----
